title: Private-submit fee model: which ceiling caps buys and sells, what base fee the affordability math uses, and per-chain escalation steps

options.name: Keep current behaviour: one 25 gwei ceiling (MEV_BUY_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI) for both legs, MEV_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI and MEV_SELL_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI without effect, base fee taken as 2 x latest, 1 gwei step on every chain
options.risk: Priority fees up to five times the documented cap; operator changes to the sell ceiling do nothing; thin-wallet private sells are refused and go public (AUD-TX-007, AUD-TX-010, AUD-TX-016).

options.name: Pass the leg to the strategies (sell ceiling and no second-sell reserve on sells), use the real latest base fee for affordability, per-chain step and floor
options.behavior_impact: Fees and refusals match the documented knobs; thin wallets keep the private sell path longer.
options.risk: A lower real-base reserve leaves less headroom if the base fee jumps between buy and sell; needs the buffer re-derived and tested per chain.

options.name: Make MEV_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI a hard cap over both legs, keep everything else as today
options.behavior_impact: The documented 5 gwei cap becomes true; private bids are lower.
options.risk: Lower private inclusion odds at busy times (the reason the 25 gwei buy ceiling was added in 21.3).

recommendation: leg-aware-real-base, and delete or redefine MEV_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI so every documented knob does what it says; correct the two alert texts.
default: Keep current behaviour until the owning phase decides (milestone contract). The findings here are S2/S3 (bounded overspend and indirect exposure), so the default can stand until Phase 24 decides.
behavior_impact: Decides how much the bot may tip per private submit and when a thin wallet must sell publicly.
needed_by: Phase 24 discussion (capital fixes, after the Phase 23 real-path proof)
